title: What words do we use for a quarter and three quarters?
description: Six fractions are written on the board, from a quarter up to two and a half, and each gets the words people use for it at home. Comparing the words across languages shows that one fraction can have many names. Keeko's raised hand ties these words to the Rig Veda.
teaching_notes: One idea: every language has its own words for the same fractions, and many of them are very old. Watch for students who think only the English words count.

source: Find out and discuss the words for fractions that are used in the different languages spoken in your home, city, or state.
video_script.why: The child learns that fractions have their own words in every language, and that the words for three quarters in Hindi and Tamil are very old.
video_script.substitution: Ask people at home and in class for their word for each fraction, and write it next to the fraction.
video_script.anchor: Six fractions written in a row, from a quarter up to two and a half, each with space for a word beside it
video_script.payoff_line: Each language has its own word for the same fraction

final_answer.value: answers vary; for example, three quarters is teen paav in Hindi and mukkaal in Tamil
final_answer.spoken: answers vary, for example three quarters is teen paav in Hindi and mukkaal in Tamil

video_script.fraction_reading: half, quarter, three quarters, one and a quarter, one and a half, two and a half; the book's word quarter is read as one fourth
never_show: the words for three quarters before the answer beat
maths_rules: 3/4 is 3 times 1/4, so it is three quarters
1 1/4 is 1 whole and 1/4; 1 1/2 is 1 whole and 1/2; 2 1/2 is 2 wholes and 1/2
the answer depends on the languages spoken, so it varies; the book's own examples: 3/4 is teen paav in colloquial Hindi and mukkaal in Tamil
video_script.design: One idea: a fraction has a different word in each language. Assumes the child has met half and quarter. No wrong idea is broken; Keeko's raised hand brings the book's note on the Rig Veda. The six fractions stay on the board to the end.
